name: Private object storage on IBM Cloud for synthetic documents
requirements: Private versioned COS bucket; existing service ID can upload, read and delete objects; no anonymous access; provider-managed encryption; candidate region au-syd; no compute, AI or private endpoint.

data.label: Existing service identity
data.description: An existing IBM Cloud IAM service ID that sits outside the provisioning scope. Its identifier is supplied as a required input. It is not created or modified here.

data.label: Synthetic document bucket
data.description: A private bucket in an existing COS instance with object versioning on, anonymous and public access blocked, and IBM-managed encryption. It holds synthetic documents only. Candidate region au-syd has not been verified. The COS instance ID is a required input.

brief.application: Design private object storage on IBM Cloud for synthetic documents. An existing service identity must upload, read and delete objects. Block anonymous access and enable versioning. Use provider-managed encryption. Use au-syd as a candidate region. No compute, AI or private network endpoint is needed for this first test. Existing account, resource group/project/COS instance and principal identifiers will be supplied separately. Draw a complete supported storage architecture with the explicit caller and access relationship. Do not deploy.

decisions.subject: design.private-ibm-cloud-object-storage-with-an-existing-service-id
decisions.title: Private IBM Cloud Object Storage with an existing service ID
decisions.context: Scope: one private versioned IBM Cloud Object Storage bucket in an existing COS instance. An existing IAM service ID gets object upload, read and delete access. Anonymous access is blocked and IBM manages the encryption keys. au-syd is a candidate region and has not been verified. There is no compute, no AI and no private endpoint. Account, COS instance and service ID identifiers will be supplied separately as inputs. This is a design only, with no deployment.
decisions.decision: Drawn while talking as design revision 2.

needs.statement: Only the existing service identity can upload, read and delete objects in the bucket. All anonymous and public access is denied.
needs.rationale: If the access scope is too broad, documents could be exposed or deleted by the wrong identity.
needs.basis: User: "An existing service identity must upload, read and delete objects. Block anonymous access"

needs.statement: Object versioning is enabled so that overwritten or deleted documents can be recovered.
needs.rationale: Because the identity can delete objects, versioning protects against accidental loss.

needs.statement: The bucket is placed in a region that meets the confirmed data-country requirement. au-syd is only a candidate until this is confirmed.
needs.rationale: The region choice decides where the data lives. The country requirement has not been stated yet.
needs.basis: User: "Use au-syd as a candidate region"
